experiment: Two variant serializations of same 4096 logical series: sorted JSON map keys vs per (series,batch) deterministic pseudorandom permutation. Map values, metric, sample values and timestamps identical in every corresponding row. Exactly same fixed series-row ordering, same wire bytes lengths, same 24 batches and cache 1MiB/3600s, same RAW_UUID TimeSeries v11, same stock binary; A/B/B/A with 4 fresh isolated servers. Stop merges for fair TAGS rows/counters. Execute full native avg_by(project) 3 warmups+6 measured per phase and independent numeric oracle. Save canonical SHA of decoded data and separate SHA of raw transmitted bytes (different by design), exact ID+tags sorted-hash, physical parts, process CPU, write_bytes, global cache hit/miss, QueryFinish CPU, native read CPU/wall.
predicted_outcomes: P1: Both modes produce exactly same logical ID/hash/physical TAGS counts and cache hit/miss counters even though encoded JSON key order varies; failure is data correctness regression or a flawed fixture.

P2: Random key order MAY increase total insert CPU due to std::sort input order and parser/cache branch behavior; a >5% mode change exceeding within-runner A/A drift warrants replication, not immediate C++ change.
P3: Similar CPU and read timing => NO_ROBUST_ORDER_EFFECT, useful rejection of a pre-sort client optimization.
